auto usage averages visible standard windows
used/remaining modes affect meter meaning and text
panel window selection and hidden-window fallback
zero and full bar fills use the entire range
logo clips preserve presentation attributes and actual fill geometry
detail popup renders usage, accounts and costs
multiple panel providers and logo-fill modes render
backend failure is visible and a later refresh recovers
preferences window opens on the isolated desktop
disable/re-enable preserves settings and restores the indicator

baseline.evidence: Shared discovery/config/plugin/source argument contracts; installed desktop launchers work outside a terminal PATH.
Manifest, metric and legacy normalization, including retained paid/supplemental metadata.
Error/recovery fixtures, timeout/cancellation contracts, actual in-flight upgrade and preferences-close cancellation. Arbitrary custom shell process trees remain untested.
Identity/order/grouping contracts, all desktop profiles, real add/rename/reorder/hide UI flows.
Private synthetic credential/config writes and stable/dev separation; config survives upgrade, reboot and uninstall.
Actual widget flows add/remove/reorder providers and grouped API/custom-command sources, set an icon and restore hidden providers. Real external authentication/setup remains provider-specific.
Standard/extra quota windows, currency, quantities, resets and clamped boundaries in contracts and native views.
Selected quota and hidden-selection fallback in contracts and native sessions.
Visible-standard mean and exhausted-primary paid fallback, including hidden paid quota.
Used/remaining percentages/fills and used-based thresholds; native screenshots and rendering contracts.
Costs, credits, code review, pace/ETA, paid currency and service status reach representative native details; optional cost failure leaves quota visible.
Visible indicators, grouped details, switches, refresh/errors/timestamps and native Plasma overview; GUI background and icon defects fixed during review.

Six rich graphical profiles cover ordered/pinned providers, components, three windows and vertical layouts. Square trays abbreviate names and control item order; Polybar remains text-only. Not every setting combination was exercised. #5–#13.

Custom threshold colors and SVG/raster rendering/fill contracts pass; light/dark preferences and representative panel themes reviewed. Tray size and Polybar's lack of image logos constrain parity. Arbitrary malformed custom icons and every theme/fill combination remain untested. #5–#13.

Six vertical layouts, Sway mixed-scale virtual outputs, two VM DPI settings, native clicks and basic keyboard actions pass. Fractional scaling, physical hotplug, screen readers and all focus/placement combinations remain. #16.
Threshold contracts plus real Dunst notification delivery and suppression in LXQt; other notification daemons remain untested.
Four pages and representative provider, appearance and tool workflows pass on both library generations at both scales and themes.
Real URL handler and XTerm/backend launch, refresh and metadata links pass. Actual provider authentication, backend/plugin installer execution and other terminals remain untested.
Service/panel restart, exact item recovery, in-flight upgrade, preferences-close cancellation and full reboot on the two Xfce VM profiles. Other desktop host/lifecycle combinations remain.
Clean install/upgrade/login/reboot/uninstall on Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora 44 Xfce x86_64; native bundle installation in all desktop labs. Other distro/session/architecture combinations remain in #16.

limitations: Square tray slots constrain text and component placement; host controls item order.
Polybar has text meters and initials, without image logos or native graphical multi-row layouts.
Full VM login lifecycle covers only Xfce on Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora 44 x86_64.
Other distro/session/version/architecture combinations, full accessibility and physical-monitor acceptance remain open.
External provider authentication and installer flows are not exercised by fixtures.
